flagged.evidence: Step 2.1 proves only that the constructed x is not in im(\widehat f). Step 3.1 then says: "Therefore \widehat f is not surjective, even though f sits in a short exact sequence. This is exactly the failure excluded by the finite-generation hypothesis." Non-surjectivity of the completion of f does not contradict exactness of the completed sequence, since f itself is not surjective. The proof must additionally show that x lies in the kernel of \widehat M -> \widehat{\operatorname{coker}(f)}; that is true here but is not stated.

[L2] asserts "For every R-module M, one has \widehat M/I^n\widehat M \cong M/I^nM" and cites cor-completion-commutes-with-finite-quotients-and-submodules. That corollary's Statement assumes "N \subseteq M be finitely generated R-modules" (lines 29-30), so it does not license the asserted universal quantifier over every R-module.

The page says that "one iterated completion collapses to the same completed object because the two adic filtrations are cofinal." Its current dependency ex-iterated-adic-completions instead has the title "Powers of an ideal give the same one-step adic completion" and proves only \widehat M^I \cong \widehat M^{I^r}, followed by the identity I+I^r=I (lines 25-50). A one-step cofinal-completion comparison does not establish an iterated-completion collapse.
